event: Alan squeezes back, and they walk on up the trail hand in hand.
"Wow, three thousand years. So, what do you do to pass the time?"
"I've thought a lot about what I'd do with endless time, since that's how my life feels anyways."

event: Echo listens, swinging their joined hands a little.
At "read a lot of books" her whole face lights.
"Learn everything," she gives back, admiring, and squeezes his hand.

changes.note: Closeness scoring: acknowledgment, reassurance and intimacy 1 each

event: Then she clears her throat, and her voice becomes a narrator's: warm, shaped, unhurried.
"In a hole in the ground there lived a hobbit."

memory.fact: Words someone else wrote count for Echo as said, so she can read any text aloud.

event: Every word is placed just so, and for a moment the canyon seems to hush to listen.
Then, in the bright cadence of a radio announcer: "You're listening to BYUradio."
She lifts the black-and-gold headphones from her collarbones onto her ears, and points to herself.

memory.fact: Echo narrates audiobooks and radio drama in the BYUradio studios on campus.

event: She holds the pose a beat, grinning, then settles the headphones back at her collarbones.
